title: How Forward Deployed Engineering is done at Decagon — Sunny Rekhi
talk_summary: Sunny Rekhi describes Decagon's forward-deployed engineering org, where the same engineers configure customer agents and feed recurring customer asks back into the product. The core lessons are restraint in one-off custom work, productizing repeated manual work into self-serve, and treating field engineers as advisors who generalize solutions across customers.

takeaways.technique: Generalize one-off requests into product features instead of patching per-customer
takeaways.what_they_do: When a customer asks for something, they check whether other customers will need it and build the general solution rather than a bespoke patch, explicitly resisting the temptation to just prompt a coding model for a quick one-off.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the scarce skill now that AI coding is so good, the scarce skill is actually exercising restraint

takeaways.technique: Productize repeated manual work into self-serve tooling
takeaways.what_they_do: After building ~25 custom integrations by hand, they built a self-serve path so customers or the agent-building team could do it without an engineer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: After like the 25th one, we're like, "I don't know how many more are coming up." Uh so, let's just like build it a self-serve way.

takeaways.technique: Specialize roles as scale grows (builder vs. product engineer)
takeaways.what_they_do: They split a single 'agent software engineer' role into 'agent builder' (model/config intuition, works in UI) and 'agent software engineer' (feeds product asks back into the platform).
takeaways.evidence_quote: we broke apart this agent software engineering role into two specialized lanes. One is the agent builder

takeaways.technique: Define success criteria in writing before starting work
takeaways.what_they_do: Before building, they nail down with the customer what success looks like — metrics, channel, ideal outcome — ideally in writing, to avoid miscommunication and rework.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want to figure out ahead of time what does success look like for the customer... ideally getting it in writing

takeaways.technique: Staff by domain to compound knowledge across similar work
takeaways.what_they_do: They staff a core group with prior experience in the same vertical so lingo, credibility, and agent-building patterns carry over to the next similar customer.

takeaways.technique: Prove value fast, then expand scope
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than boiling the ocean on a complex deployment, they scope a fast value-demonstrating slice first and expand once value is proven.
